verdict: Oracle's revenue rose 5% to $12.9B as cloud revenue grew 25% — but licensing sales fell and the stock's story stayed the backlog, with signed contracts still to deliver topping $65B.

segments.name: Cloud services & license support
segments.note: Renting Oracle's cloud, plus support for the software customers already run — the steady base of the business, and nearly three-quarters of all revenue.

segments.name: Cloud license & on-premise license
segments.note: New software licenses sold outright, for customers running Oracle on their own machines — a shrinking line as customers move to the cloud.

segments.name: Services
segments.note: Consulting and support services that help customers run Oracle products.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Building the cloud platform and the database software — up 3% YoY.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company — finance, legal and the back office, up 3% YoY.

opex.name: Amortization of intangible assets
opex.note: Writing down the value of past acquisitions over time — a non-cash charge, down 17% YoY.

opex.name: Restructuring and other
opex.note: Acquisition-related costs of $47M plus restructuring charges of $83M.

otherDetail: Interest expense of $888M on Oracle's debt pile, plus $14M of other non-operating expenses, net.
follow100Note: Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
footerNote: Oracle reports its delivery costs as 'Cloud services and license support', 'Hardware' and 'Services' expense lines; those three are combined here as cost of revenue. Segment names follow the presentation Oracle used through fiscal 2025; from fiscal 2026 Oracle regrouped its reporting into Cloud, Software, Hardware and Services.

takeaways.title: The backlog kept climbing
takeaways.text: Remaining performance obligations — work customers have signed for but Oracle has not yet delivered — climbed past $65B, more than a full year of revenue, as companies booked AI data-center capacity.

takeaways.title: Cloud infrastructure is the engine
takeaways.text: Cloud infrastructure (IaaS) revenue jumped 52% to $1.6B and cloud applications (SaaS) rose 15% to $3.2B; total cloud revenue grew 25% to $4.8B and is running at nearly a $20B annual rate.

takeaways.title: Licenses lagged, margins widened
takeaways.text: Cloud license and on-premise license revenue fell 18% as customers shifted to subscriptions, yet GAAP operating margin widened to 28% and GAAP net income rose 44% to $2.5B on a much lower tax bill.
